name: ES Incomplete Counter-Auction Relay v1
instrument: ES continuous front-month signal with one MES execution unit per slot
research_motivation: The surviving candidate family is economically consistent with accepted inventory surviving a counter-move. The rejected value-ladder test shows that monotonic center movement alone is insufficient. This hypothesis therefore requires migration, a counter-auction, and failure of that counter-auction to erase the original migration.

shared_rule.auction_center: volume-weighted mean of one-minute typical price, where typical price is (high + low + close) / 3
shared_rule.long_signal: second auction center > first auction center, while third center < second center but remains > first center
shared_rule.short_signal: second auction center < first auction center, while third center > second center but remains < first center
shared_rule.interpretation: The second auction migrates accepted value; the third auction counter-moves but cannot reclaim the first auction's center.
shared_rule.entry: one-minute open immediately following the third auction plus one adverse ES tick, in the direction of the original migration
shared_rule.stop_fill: first auction center plus one adverse ES tick
shared_rule.same_bar_rule: if the entry bar touches the stop trigger, assume the stop fills
shared_rule.survivor_exit: 90 minutes after entry, at that minute's open plus one adverse ES tick

portfolio_limits.maximum_gross_position: one MES because adjacent slots exit as the next slot enters

lesson: Incomplete correction is not scale-invariant. Repeating the midday inventory story in 30-minute auctions again isolated a 2022 opening-window effect. The original two-hour morning/two-hour lunch handoff may matter because of participant timing, not because any nested three-auction shape has predictive power. No side, year, or slot filter is permitted after observing these results.
holdout_policy: 2024-2025 was not evaluated because the frozen aggregate failed its development gates.
